data.name: Vivienne
data.gender_notes: Vivienne is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'vivus' meaning 'alive' or 'living'. The name Vivienne was given to girls born in the 6th century AD who were named after Saint Vivienne, a Christian martyr. The name Vivienne carries the meaning “Alive, living” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Vivienne usually hope their child will grow to embody alive, living and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the living spirit of God within each person.
data.etymology: Vivienne belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Alive, living.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vivienne total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: ויויאן
in_hebrew.meaning: חיה ורעננה, שם נוצרי לילדה שמחה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ויויאן מקורו בשפה הלטינית ומשמעותו 'חיה' או 'רעננה'. השם אינו מופיע ישירות בתנ'ך, אך הוא קשור למושגים של חיים ושמחה, אשר מוזכרים בכתבי הקודש. השם ויויאן הוא נוצרי ומשמש לעתים קרובות כסמל לחיים נצחיים ושמחה רוחנית.

in_greek.name: Βιβιέννη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Βιβιέννη προέρχεται από τη Λατινική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'ζων' ή 'γεμάτη ζωή'. Αν και δεν αναφέρεται άμεσα στη Νέα Διαθήκη, η έννοια της ζωής και της χαράς είναι κεντρική στο Χριστιανισμό. Το όνομα Βιβιέννη αντανακλά την πνευματική χαρά και την πληρότητα που βρίσκονται στην πίστη.

in_latin.name: Vivienne
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Vivienne originem habet in lingua Latina, significans 'vivens' seu 'plena vita'. Quamquam non directe in Scripturis apparet, conceptus vitae et gaudii sunt fundamentales in Christianismo. Nomen Vivienne exprimit gaudium spirituale et plenitudinem quae in fide inveniuntur.

in_english.name: Vivienne
in_english.meaning: Alive, full of life and joy, a symbol of spiritual vitality
in_english.long_meaning: The name Vivienne originates from Latin, meaning 'alive' or 'full of life'. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, the concept of life and joy is central to Christian faith. Vivienne reflects spiritual joy and fulfillment found in faith. Historically, the name has been used in Christian traditions to signify eternal life and happiness. It is associated with positive personality traits such as vitality, enthusiasm, and a joyful spirit.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vivienne has been popularized in various fields such as literature, arts, and media. Vivienne is a character in Arthurian legends and Shakespeare's play "The Witch of Endor". In modern times, it has been the name of several notable figures, including Vivienne Westwood, a renowned British fashion designer, and Vivienne Leigh, a famous British actress.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Vivienne signifies a connection to the divine and a reminder of the gift of life. It is a name inspired by the life and witness of a Christian martyr, and it calls to mind the potential for living a life that reflects the love and mercy of God. The name Vivienne is a powerful reminder to value the gift of life and live it with courage and faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vivienne: God is my life; divine grace in every breath I take.

historical_references.reference: Viviane was a queen of Dumnonia, a Celtic kingdom in southwest England, in the late 5th and early 6th centuries.
historical_references.context: Dumnonia was a Celtic kingdom in southwest England

historical_references.reference: Viviane was also known as the Lady of the Lake in Arthurian legend, and was said to have taught Merlin magic.

It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Hannah Vivienne in Athens, Greece credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Vivienne, which means "Alive, living". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
